newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Two Australian T-bond tenders by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Two Australian T-bond tenders by year-end.

text.p: The Australia Treasury said that two further Treasury bond tenders and a Treasury adjustable rate bond (TAB) tender can be expected before the end of the year.

"The practice of weighting (Treasury) bond issue towards the first half of the financial year is being continued and a further two tenders can be expected before the end of the current calender year," said Tony Hinton, First Assistant Secretary, Investment and Debt Division Commwealth Treasury.
Four tenders have already been held this financial year totalling A$3.0 billion out of an expected A$6.0 to A$7.0 billion of Treasury fixed coupon bond issuance.

Addressing the Australian Financial Markets Association (AFMA) in Sydney, Hinton said additional issuance into the new 2009 benchmark, first tendered on October 29, could be expected over coming tenders to help build up the level of outstandings to a liquid level.
"At this stage, there are no plans to issue an additonal new benchmark line this financial year," Hinton said.

He also said that given the small financing requirement, the Treasury was currently taken soundings from the market over whether to continue the practice of holding A$600 million to A$1.0 billion sized tenders every four to six weeks or to hold

them on more frequently, with volumes of A$200 to A$400 million. The first TABs tender for 1996/97 was also expected before the end of the year, with total issuance for the whole financial year put at A$1.0 billion.
The possible extension of the floating rate curve beyond the present four years would be considered during the financial year, Hinton said.
"At this stage, our inclination is to direct that issuance in the existing October 2000 line rather than introduce a new line with relatively limited liquidity," Hinton said.
A new 2020 indexed bond was issued on October 10 through a A$250 million tender. Total issuance for indexed bonds in 1996/97 is expected to be A$500 million to A$1.0 billion.
"Over the next few tenders, priority will be given to building up the liquidity of the new 2020 line," Hinton said.
However, there were plans to continue to issue into the 2015 line as demand and circumstances permitted, he added.
